text:
oncall-bot: 🔔 paging @channel — Production alert: KV cache size spike + continuous-batching tail latency increase. p95 generation latency up from 220ms -> 1.9s; error rate up ~1.8% on some tenants. Suspected amplification from KV cache retention growth (kv.cache.total_bytes). Impacting tenants: whale-inc (tenant_id=tn_whale_42), edge-apps (tn_edge_7). Please acknowledge and start mitigation.

ashwin: ack — I'm on it. Which region? any correlation with recent rollout?

oncall-bot: region=us-west-2, recent deploys: none in the last 45m. Feature flag runtime.batch_autotune rolled 202s ago (canary 10%).

maria: looking at metrics now — I see continuous_batch_kv_hits is low but kv.cache.evictions spiked, and kv.cache.total_objects doubled. Suggest we reduce continuous batch size and cap kv cache TTL as a live mitigation. We can do per-tenant override for whale-inc while we investigate root cause.

ashwin: agree. Can you push a per-tenant override? We want to drop max_batch_size -> 8 and kv_ttl -> 30s for the tenant. If that improves tail latency we can keep it while we debug autotuner.

maria: applying override now. CLI:

```
# per-tenant override
redwoodctl feature-flag set runtime.batch_config --tenant tn_whale_42 \
  --set '{"max_batch_size":8, "kv_ttl_seconds":30, "continuous_batch_enabled":false}'

# verify
redwoodctl feature-flag get runtime.batch_config --tenant tn_whale_42
```

deploy-bot: 🚀 per-tenant override applied for tn_whale_42 by maria. Can be rolled back with:

```
redwoodctl feature-flag unset runtime.batch_config --tenant tn_whale_42
```

jess: nice. Maria, after you apply, can you also flip the global canary back to 0% if it looks suspicious? I don't want the autotuner to keep changing things while we stabilize.

maria: done with override. Also paused the global autotuner canary (runtime.batch_autotune -> 0%). Command:

```
redwoodctl flag set runtime.batch_autotune 0 --scope global
```

ashwin: checking telemetry — p95 for tn_whale_42 falling: from 1.9s -> 480ms within 45s of the override. kv.cache.total_bytes also dropping. Error rate trending down. That's promising.

kevin: thanks folks — product wants to know customer impact. Is whale-inc seeing request failures or just latency? We should draft a short notify for support.

jess: looks like mostly latency and occasional timeouts (~0.3%); no data loss. Suggest messaging: "We observed increased request latency affecting some customers; mitigation applied; performance is improving; we will follow up with details and credits if needed." I'll ping support.

ashwin: logging runbook steps here. If latency drops to baseline for 10m, we consider this mitigated. Next actions: 1) keep per-tenant override on for whale-inc, 2) keep autotuner paused, 3) run capture of example request traces for debugging, 4) schedule root-cause follow-up and postmortem owner.

maria: collecting traces now. grep from runtime logs:

```
2026-06-11T21:24:08Z runtime[worker-7]: WARN kv_cache: size=1.9GB total_objects=1_200_123 evictions=5234 msg="cache amplification, continuous-batch balloon"
2026-06-11T21:24:10Z runtime[worker-7]: ERROR gen: tail_latency=1900ms tenant=tn_whale_42 trace_id=... context="kv miss thrash"
```

ashwin: good captures. Maria — can you also apply a conservative global fallback for extreme cases: set max_batch_size global -> 16 (was 64) as a temporary safety? I know it's broader but reduces risk until we patch tuner.

maria: applying global temporary cap now.

```
redwoodctl feature-flag set runtime.batch_config --scope global --set '{"max_batch_size":16}'
```

deploy-bot: global batch_config updated to max_batch_size=16 by maria. Note: this affects all tenants.

ashwin: timeline check — override applied at root_ts 1882503456. Current time +6m: metrics improved. Can we keep per-tenant override + global cap for now and start a canary rollback plan to re-enable autotuner only after patch validated?

maria: yes. Plan: keep overrides, collect 30m of telemetry, run patch that fixes the autotuner edge-case (limits growth when kv.size > 1GB). Once patch validated in staging, we'll canary to 10% for 15m, then 50% then 100%.

jess: I'll update incident state to "mitigated" and prepare support message. Also scheduling handoff: ashwin handed to jess at +4h for on-call wrapup.

ashwin: leaving notes for handoff — postmortem owner: maria. Action items assigned: maria (root cause debug + patch), jess (support comms + customer outreach), ashwin (follow-up rollback/rollout runbook).

kevin: product asks to proactively offer a credit to whale-inc for disruption. I'll coordinate with finance after postmortem.

deploy-bot: canary config change requested: runtime.batch_autotune -> paused, queued patch rollout job id=patch-8992. To start canary: `redwoodctl rollout start patch-8992 --canary 10% --duration 15m`.

maria: started patch in staging, tests pass. Will trigger production canary after 30m of telemetry.

oncall-bot: summary pinned: incident_id=inc_20260611_kv_amplification, status=mitigated, active_mitigations=[per-tenant override tn_whale_42, global max_batch_size=16, autotuner_paused], owners=[maria, jess, ashwin].

ashwin: handing off — I'm good to escalate if anything trends up, otherwise jess will be primary. Good job team :thumbsup:

jess: taking over. I'll keep monitoring for next 2h and check in to verify canary rollout outcome. If we see any regression after patch, revert patch with `redwoodctl rollout abort patch-8992`.

maria: noted. Captured traces and one failing request payload saved under s3://incidents/1882503456/traces.tar.gz. I'll start working the autotuner limit fix and open PR with tests.

deploy-bot: canary for patch-8992 scheduled to start at 1882505656 (in ~36m).

oncall-bot: closing page for now — mitigation applied. Mark as triaged. Follow-up: postmortem in #postmortems, owner=maria.
